canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether LLM-derived synthetic clinical judgments can improve clinical faithfulness and motor-milestone prediction of latent representations for longitudinal SMA data.
The analysis used SMArtCARE HINE-2 data from 994 children with SMA under age 12 who had more than four complete HINE-2 visits.

canonical_statement: Visits with missing HINE-2 item values were excluded, and ordinal HINE-2 items were thermometer-encoded for neural-network input.
A two-dimensional age-conditional VAE generated 20,000 unique synthetic HINE-2 profiles for surrogate-model training, with age jittered by up to 0.25 years.
Synthetic-expert labeling used pairwise forced choices among SMA types 1, 2, 3, and presymptomatic motor development, repeated under reversed label order and checked for ordinal consistency.
The LLM outputs were distilled into a differentiable surrogate network that maps a clinical profile and context to a distribution over clinical labels.
The generative-model loss added a Jensen–Shannon divergence penalty between surrogate label distributions for observed and reconstructed profiles, weighted by lambda_SE.
Longitudinal visit-level latent representations were linked with a multivariate mixed-effects model, and one-year motor-milestone prediction was evaluated with time-varying Cox regression.
Milestone prediction used patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation over 10 random seeds and reported IPCW Brier score, time-dependent AUC, and calibration error.
Gemma-4-31B achieved 89.9 for ordinal consistency percent.

canonical_statement: Internal consistency checks cannot establish that retained LLM-derived labels are clinically correct; systematic errors in prompts, label definitions, rendering, or the LLM can be distilled into the training objective.
Using a differentiable surrogate instead of the LLM directly introduces approximation error and may smooth uncertainty or decision boundaries in sparse or ambiguous profile regions.
The supervision weight is a sensitive hyperparameter: high values can overemphasize the synthetic label space and reduce reconstruction quality or downstream prediction performance.

The authors conclude that synthetic-expert supervision can connect language-based clinical judgment with probabilistic longitudinal modeling, but further clinical validation and uncertainty propagation are needed.
